name: The Scrimshank Redemption
objectiveText: Discover the fate of Junior Surveyor Scrimshank, and bring either him or his surveying equipment to Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser in Gadgetzan. Scrimshank's Surveying Gear  ( 1 )

comments.body:
Some of you need to learn right from left.

When come to the hive there will be two opening, one upper and one lower. Take the uppper opening.

You will come to a "Y" just as you enter, go LEFT.

You will enter a large round room, proceed through the tunnel (only one).

From here you will enter a large square room (butterfly shape as some call it) room with four distinct corners, go left. If you look at the mini-map, it would the North-West direction.

There it is, gaurded by one insect. Level will generally be between 47 - 49, depending on respawn.

If you are a Rogue 46+ or Druid 48+, you can stealth through easily. Rogues will find it easier to use distract to make sure the insects are looking in the other direction.

For other classes, it's pretty much a fight through. Insects are a tough bunch for their level and there are plenty of patrols inside - so keep an eye out.

I soloed this as a 47 Mage without much trouble and without dying once. Frost Nova (insta-AOE) helps a lot against the little parasites (sometimes 2 or 3) that spawn after you kill a bigger bug. Follow the steps below to find the objective:

1. Enter the Gaping Chasm region and head for the middle of the purple slime. You'll see the main entrance to the lair near the center of that region, with large raised ridges nearby.

2. When you get to the entrance, there will be two holes leading down into the lair. Take the northern-most hole. In other words, the one to your righthand side as you descend the outer ramp.

3. When you come to the first fork, just inside, take a right which will lead you to an oval-shaped room with just a few bugs between 47-49. Kill the ones in the way and make your way to the opposite side of the round room.

4. From the other side of the round room, you'll find a path that leads to a slightly larger square room. As you enter the square room, stick to the right wall and make your way into the corner guarded by a level 50 bug. The object is there, behind him, and is large enough to target from all the way across the room.

The directions given above suck if you don't have a coordinate mod installed (or, like me, don't want to just know exactly where to go by looking at a number).

The equipment is in the actual underground silithid hive itself, in the 'Gaping Chasm' area of Tanaris.  The whole place is crawling with various Hazzari Silithids.

The easiest approach I found was to enter the hive in the 'middle' of the Gaping Chasm, at the large central hole.  There is a spiral ramp leading down; go to the left at the bottom of the ramp.  Follow the tunnels (also to the left, though everything to the right is dead ends) until you reach a large X-shaped room (it's very distinctive on the map; it is referred to above as the "butterfly room", and it does sort of look like one on the minimap due to the coloring.)  The gear is in the alcove in the NW corner of that room.  It actually looks like a gnomish control console.

There are a lot of 48-50 bugs down there; visibility is poor because of the twisting tunnels, and there are a number of patrolling Hazzari Swarmers (who can overwhelm you if you don't have AOE).  If you take it slowly, you should be able to just fight one mob at a time.  If you can stealth, and you're at least L45, you can probably sneak in and only have to fight one or two enemies (maybe none if you have a way to CC the one standing by the equipment you need).

Just did this quest on a L47 BM Hunter, and it was not easy. First of all, be aware that taking the LOWER of the two ramps at the entrance allows you to enter the butterfly room' with minimal Swarmers. If you take the upper path, you'll need to face at least two.
When fighting the swarmers, the best tactic I found was to use Multishot on the first group of the little mini beetles that spawn, followed by Volley. Keep your pet healed, as those little bugs do a surpising amount of damage.
My pet died twice due to patrols ambushing me as I was fighting other mobs, but Feign Death saved the day.
Take it slow, don't rush, and pull carefully. The 'butterfly room' has several mobs, including those annoying Workers that run a mile at low health (use Concussive Shot). But most important, there's two slow, long-range patrols that come up the corridor leading to the butterfly room. They caught me from behind while I was fighting other mobs in the main chamber, which accounted for one of the pet deaths. Be aware of these patrols, and deal with them.
All in all a very tricky quest for Hunters, due to the narrow confines of the passages,  the fleeing mobs, Swarmers, and many, many patrols. Slow and steady wins the race - make your you have PLENTY of water. I can't stress this enough, you'll be  using many of your most mana-intensive abiltlities, and you're going to need it.

Soloed as a Level 50 Shadow Priest.  Take the lower cave and you don't have far to run.  The trick is to take your time and pick your way through carefully, if you go all gung ho you'll likely have issues.  Always watch your back and if you need to eat or drink, always do it at the place where the last mob you killed was standing as things can respawn quick in here.

Couple of tips for specific mobs:

Swarmers - kill the tiny swarms first or the mob will keep summoning more and they will soon overwhelm you.
Workers - these mobs run in fear when they are low on health, be sure to use any CC abilities you might have to stop them.  All I had was Mind Flay, but it worked.

The vast majority of the mobs in here spawn two parasites when they die, they have very little health but be ready for them and don't move on until they are dead.
This quest isn't too bad, just be wary of patrols and take it slow. If you're a paladin, retribution aura works like a charm against the tiny parasites.

You all save many people much time!

Frostbolt, then fireball and fireblast, then frost nova. Two steps back, fireball again and fireblast. If enemy still alive, arcane missiles. Don't forget the explosion after the kill!

Sometimes a patrol will attack as well. Then don't panic, kill the first one. Your nova should be active now. Cast it, step back, apply mageweave and if necessary, mana jade. 

Sometimes three are coming. After finishing the first. Cast nova. Mageweave then fireball, presence of mind and fireball again, then fireblast. Now cone of cold and arcane again.

If nova ready, cast and step back for evocation.

That's all :p

In response to Unicorns post. There is nothing impossible about this quest, not even close. The only mobs that are an issue are the swarmers, just like theyve always been to some classes. As a mage this was a cake walk, more time than effort. The sillithid have moderate armour and health but otherwise have no real tricks. Just be careful and patient for patrols and take each mob as they come. If you follow the plan shown and dont get bogged down in multiple mobs, you should be in and out (without hearthing or porting) in 10-15mins solo. There are two entrances but they are different areas entirely. Go to the big one at the loc posted above.

Why does everyone presume that everyone uses co-ords?  Please don't misinterpret this as being an anti co-ord post, it isn't, but personally I prefer not to use them.  I actually enjoy the game without them.  BUT.  It would be nice if more people described how to get to these places without the use of co-ords more often.  

It's nice to read about other peoples experiences on how they completed it.  I like to know the levels etc they were completed at, and to those people who provide this, thank you.  

Don't be put off by the children screaming 'I only want a co-ord, don't waste my time with descriptions'  These fools are incapable of not reading a post they aren't interested in, why take what they say seriously?

Both approaches to the info is relevant and welcomed because not everyone plays the game in the same style.

So thank you again to those who do take the time to relay thier own experiences and give details of how to reach these destinations.  I for one appreciate it greatly.
